headline: Wellington IT's letter blames an 'authorisation flaw' and mentions extortion emails; attacker still not established.
summary: 4 new sources (1 Tier 1, 3 Tier 2): North East Credit Union's own notice, the Irish Examiner, BleepingComputer and TheJournal.ie. c003 (payee fields) moves from Reported to Confirmed on the credit union's notice; c008 (Nov 15 detection) moves from Reported to Confirmed on a second independent account (Irish Examiner). Added c017 (automated script with a valid member login exploited an 'authorisation flaw', about five million requests, Reported), c018 (logs not available, Reported), c019 (extortion emails sent to Wellington and credit unions, Reported) and c020 (sector bodies' joint statement, Reported). c004, c006, c012, c013 and c014 updated; the 1.4 million and five million request figures conflict. Main answer q001 unchanged. Irish Independent not checked: access blocked. Privacy check done.
author: Research agent

headline: Wellington IT, supplier to about 40 Irish credit unions, was breached; payee details exposed, attacker not established.
summary: First draft. 6 sources (1 Tier 1, 5 Tier 2), 16 claims, 6 questions. Ireland's Department of Finance, with RTÉ, The Record and The Irish Times, establishes that an outside party got unauthorised access to saved-payee data at Wellington IT. Which fields, the 1.4 million request figure and the detection timeline are Reported. Money taken, the attacker, the member count and the method are Not established. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.
author: Research agent
